seo.title: Jonathan in the Bible: Saul's son and David's best friend
seo.description: Jonathan in plain words: the cliff at Michmash, the honey, his covenant with David, the arrows in the field, and how he died on Mount Gilboa.

band.lede: King Saul's son and David's closest friend. He climbed a cliff to take on the Philistines, and faced his father's spear for David's sake.

who: Jonathan was the eldest son of Saul, Israel's first king, and a brave soldier. With only his armour-bearer, he climbed a cliff and routed a Philistine outpost. He loved David as himself, though David would take the throne that would have been his. He saved David from his father, and died with Saul in battle on Mount Gilboa.

tidbits.text: His name means “the LORD has given”.
In Josephus's retelling, written about 93, Jonathan does not beg for his life over the honey. He tells Saul, “Nor do I desire you, father, to spare me”.

cite.text: Josephus, *Antiquities of the Jews*, book 6, chapter 6

tidbits.text: Chronicles follows his family for more than ten generations. It ends with his descendants the sons of Ulam: “mighty men of valor, archers”.

facts.label: Home
facts.text: **Gibeah** in Benjamin, his father's town. When Saul's war with the Philistines began, a thousand men were with Jonathan there.

facts.label: Family
facts.text: His father was **Saul**, Israel's first king, and his mother **Ahinoam**. His brothers were **Abinadab**, **Malchishua** and **Ish-bosheth**. His sisters were **Merab** and **Michal**, David's first wife. His son was **Mephibosheth**.

facts.label: Work
facts.text: A **soldier**, and a commander in his father's war with the Philistines.

facts.label: His weapon
facts.text: The **bow**. David's lament remembers it: “the bow of Jonathan did not retreat”.

facts.label: Also called
facts.text: **Yehonathan**, the full form of his name in Hebrew. **Ionathan**, in the Greek Bible.

facts.label: Died
facts.text: In battle with the Philistines on **Mount Gilboa**, with his father and two of his brothers.

facts.label: Buried
facts.text: First under a **tamarisk tree** at **Jabesh**. Later David moved his bones to **Zela** in Benjamin, to the tomb of his grandfather **Kish**.

facts.label: In the Bible
facts.text: **1 Samuel 13 to 31**. David mourns him in **2 Samuel 1**, and keeps his promise to him in **2 Samuel 9**.

facts.label: In art
facts.text: Often with a **bow and arrows**, for the arrows he shot to warn David. Leighton's painting here is called *Jonathan's Token to David*.

moments.title: The first blow
moments.text: Saul chose three thousand men and put a thousand of them under Jonathan at Gibeah. Then Jonathan attacked the Philistine outpost at Geba. The news went through the land in this form: “Saul has attacked an outpost of the Philistines”. The Philistines came up in force, with troops “as numerous as the sand on the seashore”. The men of Israel hid in caves and cisterns. They had almost no weapons, for the Philistines let no blacksmith work in the land. On the day of battle, only Saul and Jonathan had a sword or a spear.

moments.title: Two men and a cliff
moments.text: Jonathan said to his armour-bearer, “Come, let us cross over to the Philistine outpost on the other side.” He did not tell his father. There were steep cliffs on both sides of the pass. Jonathan set a sign: if the Philistines called them up, they would go. The men of the outpost saw them. “Look, the Hebrews are coming out of the holes in which they were hiding!” they said. “Come on up, and we will teach you a lesson!” Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, with his armour-bearer behind him, and the Philistines fell before him. Panic swept the whole Philistine camp. “Indeed, the earth quaked, and panic spread from God.” That day, “the LORD saved Israel.”

moments.title: The honey
moments.text: Saul had put the army under an oath: “Cursed is the man who eats any food before evening, before I have taken vengeance on my enemies.” The men were faint with hunger. In the forest there was honey on the ground, but no one dared to touch it. Jonathan had not heard the oath. He dipped the end of his staff into a honeycomb and ate, “and his eyes brightened.” When a soldier told him of the oath, he said, “My father has brought trouble to the land.” If the men had eaten, he said, the victory would have been far greater.

moments.title: “And now I must die?”
moments.text: Saul wanted to chase the Philistines by night. He asked God, but God did not answer him that day. Saul swore that whoever had sinned must die, “even if it is my son Jonathan”. Lots were cast, and Jonathan was taken. “I only tasted a little honey with the end of the staff that was in my hand. And now I must die?” Saul swore that he would. But the army would not allow it, and they rescued him.

moments.title: Knit together
moments.text: David came back from killing Goliath and spoke with Saul. Then “the souls of Jonathan and David were knit together, and Jonathan loved him as himself.” Jonathan made a covenant with David. He took off the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, with his tunic, his sword, his bow and his belt.

moments.title: “He has not sinned against you”
moments.text: Saul ordered Jonathan and all his servants to kill David. Jonathan warned David to hide in a field. Then he went out and spoke well of David to his father. “The king should not sin against his servant David; he has not sinned against you.” David had risked his life against Goliath, he said, so “why would you sin against innocent blood by killing David for no reason?” Saul listened and swore that David would not be put to death. Jonathan brought David back to court. The peace did not last. Saul soon threw a spear at David, and David fled.

moments.title: The empty seat
moments.text: David came to Jonathan in fear for his life. “There is but a step between me and death.” Jonathan could hardly believe it, but he said, “Whatever you desire, I will do for you.” David would hide while Jonathan sounded out his father at the feast. On the second day Saul asked where David was, and Jonathan gave David's excuse. Saul's anger burned. He cursed his son and said of David, “he must surely die!” Jonathan asked, “Why must he be put to death? What has he done?” Then Saul hurled his spear at Jonathan. Jonathan left the table in fierce anger and ate nothing that day, “for he was grieved by his father’s shameful treatment of David.”

moments.place: The field by the stone Ezel
moments.title: The arrows
moments.text: They had agreed on a sign. Jonathan would shoot arrows and send a boy to fetch them. If he called out, “the arrows are beyond you,” David must go. In the morning Jonathan went out with a small boy and shot an arrow beyond him. “Isn’t the arrow beyond you?” he called. “Hurry! Make haste! Do not delay!” The boy knew nothing. Jonathan gave him his gear and sent him back to the city. Then David came out from beside the stone and bowed three times. The two friends kissed each other and wept together, “though David wept more.”

moments.place: Horesh, in the Wilderness of Ziph
moments.title: One last meeting
moments.text: Saul hunted David day after day. David was hiding at Horesh when Jonathan came to him there “and strengthened his hand in God.” “Do not be afraid,” he said, “for my father Saul will never lay a hand on you. And you will be king over Israel, and I will be your second-in-command.” The two made a covenant before the LORD, and Jonathan went home. The Bible never shows them together again.

myths.claim: “How the mighty have fallen” is a jeer at someone brought down by their own pride.
myths.truth: It began as grief. David sang it when Saul and Jonathan were killed on Mount Gilboa, and he did not want the enemy to gloat: “Tell it not in Gath; proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice”. The line comes three times in the song. The second time, it turns to Jonathan: “Jonathan lies slain on your heights.”

circle.name: David
circle.text: His friend. Jonathan made a covenant with him three times, and saved him from Saul more than once. David mourned him as “my brother”.

circle.name: Saul
circle.text: His father, Israel's first king. Twice he was ready to kill his own son: over the honey, and at the New Moon feast, when he threw his spear at him. They died on the same day.

circle.name: His armour-bearer
circle.text: The young man, never named, who climbed the cliff at Michmash behind him and finished off the Philistines who fell.

circle.name: Mephibosheth
circle.text: His son, lame from the age of five. Chronicles calls him Merib-baal. When seven of Saul's descendants were handed over to the Gibeonites, David spared him “because of the oath before the LORD between David and Jonathan son of Saul.”

circle.name: Michal
circle.text: His sister, and David's first wife. When Saul sent men to kill David, she let him down from a window and he escaped.

circle.name: Abinadab, Malchishua and Ish-bosheth
circle.text: His brothers. Abinadab and Malchishua died beside him on Mount Gilboa. Ish-bosheth lived, and Abner, the army's commander, made him king over Israel for two years.

death.big: He died in battle with the Philistines on Mount Gilboa, with his father Saul and two of his brothers.
paras: The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons, and killed Jonathan, Abinadab and Malchishua. Saul was badly wounded by archers and fell on his own sword. “So Saul, his three sons, his armor-bearer, and all his men died together that same day.”

The next day the Philistines found the bodies, and hung them on the wall of Beth-shan. The fighting men of Jabesh-gilead marched all night to take them down. They burned the bodies, buried the bones under the tamarisk tree at Jabesh, and fasted seven days.

When the news reached David, he and his men tore their clothes. They wept and fasted until evening “for Saul and his son Jonathan”. Then David sang his lament, the Song of the Bow, and had it taught to the people of Judah.
Years later, David had the bones of Saul and Jonathan brought from Jabesh. They were buried in Benjamin, at Zela, in the tomb of Saul's father Kish.

later.title: For Jonathan's sake
later.text: Jonathan's son Mephibosheth was five when the news came. His nurse fled with him, and he fell and became lame. When David was king, he asked, “Is there anyone left from the house of Saul to whom I can show kindness for the sake of Jonathan?” He gave Mephibosheth all of Saul's land, and a place at his own table for good.

items.q: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and delightful in life, were not divided in death. They were swifter than eagles; they were stronger than lions.
I grieve for you, Jonathan, my brother. You were delightful to me; your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.
items.ctx: The song ends, “How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!”

saint.big: He has no feast day in the Catholic, Orthodox, Anglican or Lutheran calendars. But Jewish and Christian teachers alike held up his love for David as the pattern of true friendship.

churches.note: Not in Anglican or Lutheran calendars

paras: Some lists online give him 29 December. In Rome's book of martyrs, that is the day of King David. Jonathan is not in it, in the 1916 edition or the 2004 one.
The Russian Church's *Orthodox Encyclopedia* tells his story, but gives him no day of remembrance.
